chunks: Al-Hasan al-Sayqal narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام that he said:

Indeed, I truly despise the man who comes to me and asks me about the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, then says, 'Shall I add more?' as though he sees that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله fell short in something.
And indeed, I truly despise the man who has read the Qur'an, then wakes during the night but does not rise, until when it is near dawn, he gets up rushing to it with his salat (prayer).

key_terms.أَزِيدُ: shall I add more; meaning to go beyond the established practice
key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: the night, the time associated here with voluntary devotion
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, whose recitation should affect one's worship and conduct
key_terms.بِصَلَاتِهِ: with his salat (prayer), meaning he hastens to perform it near dawn
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله as the perfect model of practice
key_terms.عَمَلِ: the practice or conduct being followed
key_terms.لَأَمْقُتُ: I intensely despise; an expression of strong moral disapproval

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about adding to the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and neglecting the night prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith censures treating the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله as deficient, as though it needs personal supplementation out of suspicion of incompleteness. It also rebukes neglecting devotion in the night, especially for one connected to the Qur'an, and hurrying to prayer only at the approach of dawn.
